# CONFORMANCE

The conformance ID register. Every test name ends in its ID; a test whose
ID is not listed here fails `cargo xtask check-model`, and so does an ID
listed here with no scenario and no test (`CM-02`).

The three honesty levels (R2):

| Level | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `some-true` | A fact reproduced from an authority. **Not established here.** |
| `build` | Constructed here and validated against its oracle. Evidence, not a proof. |
| `open` | Measured and reported. **Never asserted.** |

`cargo xtask audit-limits` fails if a shipped crate returns `Result` over an
error type not registered for it in `model/failures.toml`, if a registered type
is not a closed enum whose variants are exactly its rows, or if the crate does
not forbid `unwrap`, `expect` and `panic!` (R5).

## engine

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EN-01` | `build` | The kernel client writes each request exactly as the kernel examples have it and reads every answer the kernel gives |
| `EN-02` | `build` | A safetensors header is read into its tensors in file order, with every tensor byte range accepted by the kernel |
| `EN-03` | `build` | A model config is read into the preflight question: a named family is recognised, every missing required key is counted, and an unsupported activation is flagged |
| `EN-04` | `build` | An ONNX model's default-domain opset, its nodes' operators in file order and the tensors its graph carries are read from the file, and fields the preflight does not need are stepped over |
| `EN-05` | `build` | The operators an ONNX model names that a builder does not implement are counted into the kernel's import question, and reported each once in the order they first appear |
| `EN-06` | `some-true` | A buffer's label is the BLAKE3 hash of its bytes, as the published test vectors give it |
| `EN-07` | `build` | A download's label and length do not depend on how its bytes were split into chunks |
| `EN-08` | `build` | A download is admitted exactly when the kernel admits the label and length it arrived with against the ones the archive names, and a refusal carries the kernel's verdict |

## kernel

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KN-05` | `build` | A buffer is admitted exactly when its expected and observed labels are equal and its declared and observed lengths are equal |
| `KN-06` | `build` | A tensor byte range is accepted exactly when it starts at or after the previous tensor end and ends within the file |
| `KN-08` | `build` | The decode bucket is at least what is needed, never above the maximum, and never below the current bucket |
| `KN-09` | `build` | A turn token budget never exceeds the context that remains and never exceeds the request |
| `KN-02` | `build` | A model is supported or derived exactly when no required key is missing, no unsupported feature is flagged and the manifest fits, and only then may weights download |
| `KN-04` | `build` | The quantisation tier chosen fits in memory whenever any tier does, and more memory never lowers it |
| `KN-11` | `build` | A requested dimension is bound exactly when it lies within its bounds, to a size at least the request and never above the upper bound |
| `KN-07` | `build` | A proposed trim is accepted exactly when what remains fits the context and restoring the newest dropped pair would not |
| `KN-03` | `build` | A proposed stage plan is accepted exactly when its stage fits the memory budget, is the largest that does, and its stages cover every layer once |
| `KN-01` | `build` | Each working state is entered from exactly one state by exactly one event, failed is left only by reset, and every other step is refused |
| `KN-10` | `build` | A graph is importable exactly when its opset lies within the implemented window and no operator is unimplemented, and a wider window never makes an importable graph unimportable |

## Public failures

Every way a shipped crate can fail, from `model/failures.toml`. Each row has a
negative scenario and a test that names its variant; the gate checks the name,
not that the test provokes the failure.

| ID | Crate | Failure | Condition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FL-01` | `model-reader` | `HeaderError::TooShortForLength` | The file has fewer than the eight bytes that carry the header length |
| `FL-02` | `model-reader` | `HeaderError::HeaderExceedsFile` | The header length the file declares does not fit inside the file |
| `FL-03` | `model-reader` | `HeaderError::NotJson` | The header bytes are not a JSON object |
| `FL-04` | `model-reader` | `HeaderError::TensorNotDescribed` | A header entry is not an object carrying a dtype, a shape of whole numbers and a pair of data offsets |
| `FL-05` | `model-reader` | `HeaderError::OffsetsDoNotRunForward` | A tensor ends before it starts |
| `FL-06` | `model-reader` | `HeaderError::RangeRefused` | The kernel did not accept a tensor byte range |
| `FL-07` | `model-reader` | `ConfigError::NotJson` | The config bytes are not a JSON object |
| `FL-08` | `onnx-preflight` | `OnnxError::Truncated` | A field runs past the end of the file |
| `FL-09` | `onnx-preflight` | `OnnxError::NumberTooLong` | A variable-length number does not end within the ten bytes that carry sixty-four bits |
| `FL-10` | `onnx-preflight` | `OnnxError::UnknownEncoding` | A field says it is encoded a way the format does not define, so its end cannot be found |
| `FL-11` | `onnx-preflight` | `OnnxError::NameNotText` | A name the preflight reads is not text |
| `FL-12` | `onnx-preflight` | `OnnxError::NoGraph` | The model carries no graph |
| `FL-13` | `onnx-preflight` | `OnnxError::NoDefaultOpset` | The model declares no opset for the default domain |
| `FL-14` | `download` | `DownloadError::LabelNotHex` | A label an archive names is not sixty-four lower-case hexadecimal digits |
| `FL-15` | `download` | `DownloadError::Refused` | The kernel did not admit the buffer that arrived |
